campaign.scope: Pilot: one W128,350000-arrival35-second correctness/full-checkpoint validation with the unchanged600-second outer process deadline.

modeContext.scope: Runner count is a configuration expectation: DEDICATED includes sender, receiver, conductor and native-resource runners. Observed TIDs/CPU are retained under raw kernel-truncated comm names; no name is expanded into an invented role.

arrivalWindow.scope: Load-generator UTC origin is approximate; wall clocks are not verified synchronized. Only interior adjacent samples are differenced; monotonic time determines every rate. A lack of samples is unavailable, never a zero-CPU/zero-drop claim.

cgroupQuotaAndThrottling.scope: Current visible cgroup leaf, shared with sampler and other processes; node2 also contains the load JVM. CPU usage and throttling counters are joined only across adjacent whole-collection-interior samples with the same version/path/quota. Nanosecond counters remain nanoseconds; cpuPeriods/throttledPeriods are counts. Missing/reset counters remain unavailable, never zero. Visible quota is an upper bound, not dedicated cores; hidden ancestors and physical host contention are not measured. Aggregate spare quota does not establish spare capacity in any one thread.

csvArchiveEvidence.scope: Attribution computation reads result/observer JSON and needs no restored plaintext CSV. Gzip streams are read through their CRC and independently hashed after decompression without writing plaintext. Manifest files retain their own exact hashes; a manifest hash alone is not claimed as a semantic comparison to the independently computed raw hash. CSV outcome/latency row audit is separate.

observerCapCoverage.scope: Actual selected whole-collection-interior samples, not an assumption from worker count. A bounded scan cannot establish the total beyond its cap; missing counts/flags/read metrics remain unavailable. No truncation and no read errors are separate checks. Counts below 1024 TIDs/4096 FDs are observed scan coverage, not a future resource-capacity claim.

observer.scope: Mean per-sample collector process CPU cost divided by configured cadence, not an observer-off comparison. Per-collection cost excludes JSON serialization/flush and idle; the complete observer's total CPU includes other phases. Ratio to load CPU uses independently sampled local aggregate telemetry intervals and is approximate.

threads.scope: CPU joins require identical process identity and TID/startTicks; new/disappeared threads contribute no guessed CPU. Thread-name groups can combine many instances and kernel-truncated names. schedstat/wchan only cover the collector's selected top16 threads; wchan=0 can mean running or unavailable, and zero schedstat can mean disabled instrumentation. This does not identify a unique causal bottleneck.

udpSockets.scope: Only verified owned PID sockets with fd/inode ownership rechecked by the collector. Adjacent joins require identical process/family/inode/localbind and an overlapping fd set. Newly observed counters are not counted as arrival-window drops. Disappearance is observed absence, not a certified close; gaps, races and fd caps can hide sockets. Queue gauges are kernel-accounting bytes, not packets or effective SO_RCVBUF capacity. Drops are observed socket drop-counter increments, not business-command losses or proof of the unique loss mechanism; resets/wraps are excluded.

recorderCounters.samplingScope: CapacityCounters records timestamp after the counter scan; samplingNanos spans the scan and timestamp construction. Conservatively require timestamp-samplingNanos >= arrival start and timestamp <= arrival end. The frozen helper then differences first/last identical counter registrations over elapsedNanos, which is local monotonic time at scan start. This cumulative-counter coverage may span missed interior observations, unlike adjacent-pair thread/socket CPU coverage. Counter values and position differences are non-atomic; no exact lag or physical disk service-time inference. Archive type107 is cumulative wall time in the write path including write+force+descheduling; it is not pure fsync latency.
recorderCounters.scope: Only unchanged counter id + registration id + type + label identities are differenced; missing/reused registrations are not assumed zero. Positions identified by label/type and log stream 100. Follower receive-HWM is distinct from leader append position. Position differences are signed non-atomic observations, not exact lag or fsync durability proof.

workerAndRetentionContext.scope: Worker count also changes aggregate FIFO capacity at fixed per-worker queue size. This is a finite client/concurrency/buffering-path experiment. Global cached-result retention remains bounded by the declared 100k profile limit and per-producer retention by 1024 where verified in configuration; 350k measured commands do not imply retaining every result indefinitely. Configuration fields missing from evidence remain null.

reproduction.scope: Only the pilot is requested by default. Formal W128/W256 requires the explicit cohort argument; absent/incomplete groups have no manufactured measured point.

scope: Only the explicitly requested full-350k-profile pilot or formal W128/W256 cohorts are included; no absent W256 capacity is inferred. A new common node/load artifact, maxsessions256, SHARED node driver, shared client driver and requested receive buffer131072 define this experiment. It is not merged with the earlier 190k-profile driver, buffer or threading matrices. Frozen whole-collection/identity/socket/CnC/cgroup rules are reused. Changing workers also changes aggregate FIFO slots, Aeron/client/thread/socket resources and potential cache working set; it is not a pure server-engine optimization. Read failures/caps/gaps remain explicit. Finite observation is not sustained capacity, monotonic capacity or proof of a unique bottleneck.
